title: Ride with GPS Launches 3D Maps
content:
Ride with GPS recently announced the addition of 3D Maps, now live on the web and in the mobile app…

Flat maps have always forced riders to imagine the parts that matter most: the massive switchbacking climb and the ridge that drops into the valley. A contour line or a patch of terrain shading only goes so far. 3D Maps fundamentally changes that, letting riders tilt, rotate, and zoom into any route to visualize the terrain the way they’ll actually experience it.

3D Maps

3D Maps isn’t just a cosmetic upgrade. It completely transforms the way riders prepare for and experience routes, ultimately leading to better rides. The feature is built around three ways riders already use the map:

  • Preview in 3D — see the shape of a climb or descent before committing to a route, then tack on other tools like Community Photos, Heatmaps, and Advanced Layers to get a complete read on what to expect.
  • Plan in 3D — visually spot the tough sections right away and build a route to incorporate some extra climbing (or to avoid it entirely); regardless, planning in 3D makes the process much more fun and engaging.
  • Navigate in 3D — get real terrain context while riding, on a commute across town or a tour across the mountains, all while getting turn-by-turn directions to guide the way.

Riders aren’t locked into one look, either. 3D Maps work across Ride with GPS Cycle, OSM-based maps, ESRI Topo, and USGS-based styles, with satellite imagery available on mobile for even more terrain detail.

Different map styles offer unique information that can be critical to the route planning process for a specific area or style of riding. For a lot of riders, being able to analyze terrain using their preferred map style, as well as switching between others, gives them complete confidence in what to expect for the ride ahead.

3D Maps is live today on the web and in the Ride with GPS mobile app.
